questions.title: Circle Geometry — Reasons & the Tan-Chord Theorem

subQuestions.label: 1(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
O is the centre of the circle ABCDE. AF = FE. AG is a tangent to the circle at A. $O\hat{A}E = 40°$.

Complete the table by filling in the appropriate reason for each of the given statements, in the order given: OA = OE; $\hat{E}_1 = 40°$; $\hat{D} = 140°$; $\hat{F}_1 = 90°$; $\hat{A}_1 = 50°$; $\hat{B} = 50°$; $A\hat{O}E = 100°$.
subQuestions.memoText:
OA = OE — radii.
$\hat{E}_1 = 40°$ — angles opposite equal sides (radii).
$\hat{D} = 140°$ — opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.
$\hat{F}_1 = 90°$ — line from the centre bisects a chord (perpendicular to the chord).
$\hat{A}_1 = 50°$ — tangent $\perp$ radius.
$\hat{B} = 50°$ — tan-chord theorem.
$A\hat{O}E = 100°$ — angle at centre $= 2 \times$ angle at circle (or interior angles of $\triangle$).

subQuestions.label: 1(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Use the diagram below to prove the statement that says: 'The acute angle formed by a chord and a tangent at the point of contact is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.'

Required to prove: $\hat{A}_1 = \hat{B}$.
subQuestions.memoText:
Construction: draw radii OA and OC.
$O\hat{A}C = 90° - \hat{A}_1$ (tangent $\perp$ radius).
$O\hat{C}A = 90° - \hat{A}_1$ (angles opposite equal sides — radii OA = OC).
$A\hat{O}C = 180° - (90° - \hat{A}_1) - (90° - \hat{A}_1) = 2\hat{A}_1$ (interior angles of $\triangle$).
$\hat{B} = \dfrac{1}{2}A\hat{O}C = \hat{A}_1$ (angle at centre $= 2 \times$ angle at circle).
$\therefore \hat{A}_1 = \hat{B}$.

subQuestions.label: 2(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
PARM is a parallelogram with $P\left(-3; \dfrac{9}{2}\right)$, $A(3; 2)$ and $M(-3; -2)$. The diagonals of the parallelogram intersect at the origin. $\theta$ is the angle of inclination of line AM.

Determine the co-ordinates of R.
subQuestions.memoText: R is opposite P, and the diagonals bisect at the origin, so $R = (3; -\dfrac{9}{2})$.

subQuestions.label: 2(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine, in simplest surd form, the distance AM.

subQuestions.label: 2(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the size of $\theta$.

subQuestions.label: 2(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the equation of the line parallel to AM passing through P, in the form $y = mx + c$.

subQuestions.label: 2(e)
subQuestions.questionText: Prove that PARM is a rhombus. An appropriate reason must be given in the conclusion.
subQuestions.memoText:
$PM = \sqrt{(-3 - (-3))^2 + \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - (-2)\right)^2} = \dfrac{13}{2} = 6{,}5$ units.
$MR = \sqrt{(-3 - 3)^2 + \left(-2 - \left(-\dfrac{9}{2}\right)\right)^2} = \sqrt{36 + \dfrac{25}{4}} = 6{,}5$ units.
$PM = MR$, so PARM is a rhombus (a parallelogram with adjacent sides equal).
(Alternatively: $m_{PR} = \dfrac{\frac{9}{2} + \frac{9}{2}}{-3 - 3} = -\dfrac{3}{2}$; $m_{MA} \times m_{PR} = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = -1$, so the diagonals bisect at $90°$ — a parallelogram with perpendicular diagonals is a rhombus.)

subQuestions.label: 3(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A circle with centre N has the equation $x^2 - 2x + y^2 + 2y - 3 = 0$. JK is a tangent at K.

Determine the centre and the radius length of circle N.

subQuestions.label: 3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the co-ordinate K (the point where the circle meets the $x$-axis on the negative side).

subQuestions.label: 3(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the equation of the tangent JK.

subQuestions.label: 3(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the size of $K\hat{L}M$. A relevant reason must be given.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\tan\theta = 2$ (gradient of the tangent JK / chord KM), so $\theta = 63{,}43°$.
$\hat{L} = 63{,}43°$ (tan-chord theorem).

questions.title: Circle Geometry — Similar Triangles in a Semicircle

subQuestions.label: 4(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Circle with centre O has a diameter of 8 units, LM = 4 units and $LN \perp MP$.

Determine $\hat{M}$.
subQuestions.memoText: $\hat{M} = 90°$ (angle in a semi-circle — LN is a diameter).

subQuestions.label: 4(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Prove: $\triangle$LMN ||| $\triangle$LPM.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle$LMN and $\triangle$LPM:
$\hat{L} = \hat{L}$ (common).
$\hat{M} = \hat{P}_1$ (both $= 90°$).
$\hat{M}_1 = \hat{N}$ (third angle).
$\therefore \triangle$LMN $\;|||\;$ $\triangle$LPM (AAA).

subQuestions.label: 4(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine LP.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\dfrac{LM}{LP} = \dfrac{MN}{PM} = \dfrac{LN}{LM}$ (similar triangles, sides in proportion).
$LM^2 = LP \times LN$
$4^2 = LP \times 8$
$LP = 2$ units

subQuestions.label: 5(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Sketched is the graph of $f(x) = \sin bx$ for $x \in [-180°; 180°]$, showing two complete waves.

Determine the value of $b$.
subQuestions.memoText: Period $= \dfrac{360°}{b} = 180° \Rightarrow b = 2$

subQuestions.label: 5(b)
subQuestions.questionText: State the period of $f$.

subQuestions.label: 5(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Sketch the graph of $g(x) = -2\cos x$ on the same set of axes as $f$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$g$: reflected cosine curve, amplitude 2. Maximum $2$ at $x = \pm 180°$; minimum $-2$ at $x = 0°$; $x$-intercepts at $x = \pm 90°$; $y$-intercept $(0; -2)$.
Marks: cos shape; consistent amplitude; correct $x$- and $y$-cuts.

subQuestions.label: 5(d)
subQuestions.questionText: State the amplitude of $g$.

subQuestions.label: 5(e)
subQuestions.questionText: State the general solution for $f(x) = g(x)$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\sin 2x = -2\cos x \Rightarrow 2\sin x\cos x + 2\cos x = 0 \Rightarrow 2\cos x(\sin x + 1) = 0$.
$\cos x = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = 90° + k\cdot 180°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$ (the case $\sin x = -1$ is included).

subQuestions.label: 5(f)(1)
subQuestions.questionText: If $x \in [-180°; 180°]$, determine the values for $x$ where $f(x) \geq g(x)$.

subQuestions.label: 5(f)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: If $x \in [-180°; 180°]$, determine the values for $x$ where $\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)} < 0$.

subQuestions.label: 5(f)(3)
subQuestions.questionText: If $x \in [-180°; 180°]$, determine the values for $x$ where $g'(x) > 0$.
subQuestions.memoText: $g(x) = -2\cos x$, so $g'(x) = 2\sin x > 0$ where $\sin x > 0$: $x \in (0°; 180°)$.

subQuestions.label: 5(g)
subQuestions.questionText: If $g$ is shifted 2 units up and 45° to the right, write down the new equation for $g$ in the form $y = \ldots$

subQuestions.label: 6(a)(1)
subQuestions.questionText:
Given $\sin 40° = \dfrac{p}{4}$.

Determine $\sin 50° \cdot \cos 10° - \cos 50° \cdot \sin 10°$ in terms of $p$.

subQuestions.label: 6(a)(2)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine $\cos^2 20° - \sin^2 20°$ in terms of $p$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$= \cos 2(20°) = \cos 40°$.
With $\sin 40° = \dfrac{p}{4}$ (opposite $= p$, hypotenuse $= 4$), the adjacent side is $\sqrt{16 - p^2}$.
$\cos 40° = \dfrac{\sqrt{16 - p^2}}{4}$

subQuestions.label: 6(a)(3)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine $\tan 50°$ in terms of $p$.
subQuestions.memoText: $\tan 50° = \dfrac{\sin 50°}{\cos 50°} = \dfrac{\cos 40°}{\sin 40°} = \dfrac{\sqrt{16 - p^2}}{p}$

subQuestions.label: 6(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
In $\triangle$ABC: AB = 10 units, BC = 12 units and $A\hat{B}C = 60°$.

Determine the length of AC.

subQuestions.label: 7(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows the salaries of 10 employees, where $x$ is the number of years the employee has worked at the company and $y$ is the monthly salary in thousands of rands:

| $x$ | 1 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 3 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 |
| $y$ | 45 | 5 | 15 | 20 | 15 | 25 | 20 | 35 | 43 | 45 |

Use your calculator to determine the equation of the line of best fit in the form $y = A + Bx$.

subQuestions.label: 7(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Draw the line of best fit on the scatter plot above, showing the $y$-intercept and the co-ordinate $(\bar{x}; \bar{y})$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$(\bar{x}; \bar{y}) = (4{,}5;\ 26{,}8)$; $y$-intercept at $(0; 13{,}98)$. Draw the line through both points.
Marks: $\bar{x}$; $\bar{y}$; $y$-intercept; line through $(\bar{x}; \bar{y})$ and the $y$-intercept.

subQuestions.label: 7(c)
subQuestions.questionText: By using your answer in (b), determine the salary of an employee who has been working at the company for 4 years.

subQuestions.label: 7(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the correlation coefficient for the above data.

subQuestions.label: 7(e)
subQuestions.questionText: Circle the outlier on the graph.
subQuestions.memoText: The point $(1; 45)$ — an employee with 1 year of service earning R45 000. Circled on the diagram.

subQuestions.label: 7(f)
subQuestions.questionText: If this outlier is removed from the data, discuss the effect it will have on the correlation coefficient.
subQuestions.memoText: $r$ will increase (the correlation becomes stronger / more positive).

subQuestions.label: 8(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Study the cumulative frequency curve, which ends at a cumulative frequency of 120.

If the data for the class intervals above 70 are removed from the curve, determine the difference between the original median and the new median result.
subQuestions.memoText:
Original median at cumulative frequency $\dfrac{120}{2} = 60$: read off $\approx 62$.
After removing the intervals above 70, the new total is 100; new median at cumulative frequency $\dfrac{100}{2} = 50$: read off $\approx 60$.
Difference $= 62 - 60 = 2$.

subQuestions.label: 8(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Study the box-and-whisker plot. Will the mean be bigger or smaller than the median? Explain.
subQuestions.memoText: The data is skewed left (negatively skewed), so the mean will be smaller than the median: $\bar{x} < Q_2$.

subQuestions.label: 8(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Given three numbers 4, 8 and $p$. Using the table with $x$: $4$, $8$, $p$; $x - \bar{x}$: $-3$, $\ldots$; $(x - \bar{x})^2$: $\ldots$, determine the numerical value of $p$ and the standard deviation of the three numbers.

questions.title: Circle Geometry — Two Semicircles & Congruent Triangles

subQuestions.label: 9(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Two equal semi-circles are drawn. AC = CD = 26 units and AB = 10 units. AC and DC are tangents to circles CFD and ABC respectively. $GE \perp FD$.

Prove that EG // FC.
subQuestions.memoText:
$D\hat{F}E = 90°$ (angle in a semi-circle).
$D\hat{E}G = 90°$ (given — GE $\perp$ FD).
So $D\hat{F}E = D\hat{E}G$.
$\therefore$ EG // FC (converse — corresponding angles equal).

subQuestions.label: 9(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Prove that $\triangle$ABC $\equiv$ $\triangle$CFD and hence that CF is 10 units.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle$ABC and $\triangle$DFC:
$\hat{C}_1 = \hat{D}$ (tan-chord theorem).
$\hat{C}_2 = \hat{A}$ (tan-chord theorem).
AC = CD = 26 (given).
$\therefore \triangle$ABC $\equiv$ $\triangle$CFD (AAS).
$\therefore$ AB = CF = 10 units.

subQuestions.label: 9(c)
subQuestions.questionText: If it is further given that 3BA = 5DE, show that FE = 18 units.
subQuestions.memoText:
$3(10) = 5DE \Rightarrow DE = 6$.
$FD^2 = 26^2 - 10^2 = 576$ (Pythagoras), so $FD = 24$.
$FE = FD - DE = 24 - 6 = 18$ units.

subQuestions.label: 9(d)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the value of GC.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\dfrac{CG}{26} = \dfrac{18}{24}$ (proportion theorem — EG // FC)
$CG = \dfrac{18 \times 26}{24} = 19{,}5$ units

subQuestions.label: 10(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A, B, C, H and D all lie on the circumference of the circle. BGEHF is a straight line, and $\dfrac{AC}{DF} = \dfrac{CD}{FE} = \dfrac{AD}{DE}$.

Give a reason why $\triangle$ACD ||| $\triangle$DFE.
subQuestions.memoText: The three pairs of corresponding sides are in proportion (SSS similarity).

subQuestions.label: 10(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Prove that DF is a tangent to the circle at D.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{D}_1 = \hat{A}$ (equiangular — corresponding angles of the similar triangles $\triangle$ACD ||| $\triangle$DFE).
$\therefore$ DF is a tangent to the circle at D (converse of the tan-chord theorem).

subQuestions.label: 10(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Prove that GCFD is a cyclic quadrilateral.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{C} = \hat{F}$ (equiangular — the similar triangles).
$\therefore$ GCFD is a cyclic quadrilateral (converse — angles in the same segment equal).

subQuestions.label: 11(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
$\triangle$ABC is in the horizontal plane, with BC = 10 units, $A\hat{C}B = 2\theta - 90°$ and $A\hat{B}C = 180° - \theta$. The angle of inclination from A to D is $\theta$. $\triangle$ACD is in the vertical plane, with CD = 15 units.

Show that $AC = 10\tan\theta$.
subQuestions.memoText:
$C\hat{A}B = 180° - (2\theta - 90°) - (180° - \theta) = 90° - \theta$ (interior angles of $\triangle$).
Sine rule in $\triangle$ABC: $\dfrac{AC}{\sin(180° - \theta)} = \dfrac{10}{\sin(90° - \theta)}$
$AC = \dfrac{10\sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = 10\tan\theta$

subQuestions.label: 11(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Hence, determine the size of $\theta$ if $\theta \in [0°; 90°]$.
subQuestions.memoText:
In $\triangle$ACD: $\tan\theta = \dfrac{DC}{AC} = \dfrac{15}{10\tan\theta}$
$\tan^2\theta = \dfrac{15}{10} = \dfrac{3}{2}$
$\tan\theta = \pm 1{,}22\ldots$
$\theta = 50{,}77°$

subQuestions.label: 12(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
Prove the following using the fundamental trigonometric identities:

$$\dfrac{\cos(360° - 2x) - \cos(180° + x)}{\sin 2x - \cos(90° - x)} = \dfrac{\cos x + 1}{\sin x}$$
subQuestions.memoText:
Numerator: $\cos(360° - 2x) - \cos(180° + x) = \cos 2x + \cos x = (2\cos^2 x - 1) + \cos x = 2\cos^2 x + \cos x - 1 = (2\cos x - 1)(\cos x + 1)$.
Denominator: $\sin 2x - \cos(90° - x) = 2\sin x\cos x - \sin x = \sin x(2\cos x - 1)$.
LHS $= \dfrac{(2\cos x - 1)(\cos x + 1)}{\sin x(2\cos x - 1)} = \dfrac{\cos x + 1}{\sin x}$ = RHS.

subQuestions.label: 12(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Determine the general solution for:

$$\dfrac{\cos 2x + 1}{\sin 2x} = 1$$
subQuestions.memoText:
$\dfrac{2\cos^2 x - 1 + 1}{2\sin x\cos x} = 1$
$\dfrac{2\cos^2 x}{2\sin x\cos x} = 1$
$\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} = 1 \Rightarrow \tan x = 1$
$x = 45° + k\cdot 180°$, $k \in \mathbb{Z}$

questions.title: Analytical Geometry — Touching Circles & a Tangent

subQuestions.label: 13(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A circle with centre $C(a; b)$ and a circle with centre E and equation $(x - 9)^2 + (y - 10)^2 = r^2$ are drawn. CE = 25 units and is parallel to the $x$-axis. F is the point of tangency between the two circles.

Determine the co-ordinates of C.
subQuestions.memoText:
E is $(9; 10)$. Since CE = 25 and is parallel to the $x$-axis, C has the same $y$-coordinate: $b = 10$, and $a = 9 - 25 = -16$.
$C(-16; 10)$

subQuestions.label: 13(b)
subQuestions.questionText: If it is further given that ED = 20 units and is a tangent to the larger circle at D, determine the equation of the circle with centre C.
subQuestions.memoText:
$\hat{D} = 90°$ (tangent $\perp$ radius — CD $\perp$ ED).
$CD^2 = CE^2 - ED^2 = 25^2 - 20^2 = 225$ (Pythagoras), so $CD = 15$ (the radius of circle C).
$(x + 16)^2 + (y - 10)^2 = 225$

subQuestions.label: 13(c)
subQuestions.questionText: Determine the possible values of the radius ($r$) of circle E, such that the two circles will not touch or intersect.
subQuestions.memoText:
Distance between centres $= 25$; radius of C $= 15$.
The circles do not touch or intersect when $15 + r < 25$ (separate) or $r - 15 > 25$ (E contains C):
$r \in (0; 10)$  or  $r \in (40; \infty)$

subQuestions.label: 14(a)
subQuestions.questionText:
A stadium (a rectangle with a semicircle on each of a pair of opposite sides) is drawn on the Cartesian plane. All points on the circumference of the stadium are $2\sqrt{2}$ units from the line AB, with $A(4; 0)$ and $B(12; 8)$.

Determine the co-ordinates of P and Q, which lie on the circumference of the figure and are equidistant from A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
P and Q lie on the perpendicular bisector of AB, at distance $2\sqrt{2}$ from the midpoint $M_{AB}(8; 4)$.
$m_{AB} = 1$, so $m_{PQ} = -1$: $y - 4 = -1(x - 8) \Rightarrow y = -x + 12$.
$MP^2 = (x - 8)^2 + (y - 4)^2 = (2\sqrt{2})^2 = 8$; substituting $y = -x + 12$:
$(x - 8)^2 + (-x + 8)^2 = 8 \Rightarrow 2(x - 8)^2 = 8 \Rightarrow (x - 8)^2 = 4 \Rightarrow x = 10$ or $x = 6$.
$P(6; 6)$ and $Q(10; 2)$.

subQuestions.label: 14(b)
subQuestions.questionText: A capsule (a cylinder with hemispherical ends) is created when the stadium in question (a) is revolved around the line AB. With the formula $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$ for a sphere, determine the volume in units cubed of this capsule.
subQuestions.memoText:
Radius $r = 2\sqrt{2}$; cylinder length $H = AB = \sqrt{(12 - 4)^2 + (8 - 0)^2} = \sqrt{128} = 8\sqrt{2}$.
$V = \pi r^2 H + \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3 = \pi(2\sqrt{2})^2 (8\sqrt{2}) + \dfrac{4}{3}\pi(2\sqrt{2})^3$
$V \approx 379{,}13$ units$^3$
